title: Four times the input length with an explicit sublinear loss

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"Set f_0=0. For n>=1 let k be the least prime exceeding ceil((24/25)*n^(3/5)). Return 0 if k>=n. The last k input bits specify the coefficients of a monic degree-k binary polynomial h below its leading term. Pad the first N=n-k bits on the right with zeros into r=ceil(N/k) blocks X_j, least-degree coefficient first, in F_2[Z]/(h). For j=1,...,r set u_j=r+1-j. Output the constant coefficient of the elementary symmetric polynomial of degree ceil(sqrt(r)) on the r values X_j^(2^u_j-1), using the degree-<k representative. The selector coefficients are in increasing degree order.","guarantee":{"kind":"eventual_lower_bound","leading":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"remainder":{"kind":"explicit","terms":[{"coefficient":{"denominator":"4","numerator":"61"},"exponent":{"denominator":"5","numerator":"4"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}}]}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total polynomial-time family, with an empty-witness NP verifier, there is an N_0 such that at every integer actual input length n>=N_0, every exact nonuniform single-output full-B2 circuit for f_n has at least 4*n-(61/4)*n^(4/5) gates. In particular liminf C_B2(f_n)/n >= 4 over all integer lengths.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v2"}

claims: On fixing the modulus selector to any monic irreducible at a length with k<n, the data restriction takes both values on each binary affine space of dimension D>k*t+r*(r+1)/2, with k,r,t as in proof.md.
For 1<=d<=N, a Boolean function on N inputs that takes both values on every d-dimensional binary affine space requires at least 4*N-10*d gates in the full B2 model.
